common_name: Takeda Nishiki Variegated Japanese Clethra ('First Snow' Summersweet Relative)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring so roots establish before summer heat, siting them in humus-rich, evenly moist, acidic soil where the variegated foliage gets some shelter from harsh afternoon sun to prevent leaf scorch.

directions: This large, tree-like selection of Japanese clethra is grown chiefly for its foliage, which emerges flushed pink and matures to a bold, irregular splash of white and cream over green, then colors up again with red and gold tones in autumn. Discovered in Japan and later distributed under the trade name First Snow, it retains the species' arching midsummer racemes of fragrant white flowers and its winter-interest exfoliating bark, but the variegation makes it a slower, more sun-sensitive grower than plain-leaved forms. Give it consistently moist, acidic, well-drained soil and dappled shade, especially in warmer zones, and prune only lightly after flowering to preserve its naturally layered branching. Because variegated shoots can be less vigorous, remove any branches that revert to solid green so they do not overtake the patterned growth.
